children: Bitcoin News said on X that security researcher @cyberscrilla found a fake Ledger website and app at the top of Google search results, designed to trick users into revealing their 24-word recovery phrases. According to Odaily, Google data showed the site received more than 1 million visits in the past 30 days.

Zscaler previously found malicious Google ads impersonating Ledger and redirecting users to a fake wallet verification page in a September investigation. Ledger is also investigating a suspected wallet theft involving customers of Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, with losses estimated at $86 million.

title: Fake Ledger Website Appears at Top of Google Search Results in Suspected $86 Million Wallet Theft Case
